answer: Operator Liability Prism: each new identity’s actions are routed through a mirror of its sponsor’s reputation, so misbehavior by a sybil debits the sponsor’s standing rather than the disposable wallet. A kernel rule caps every sponsor at a fixed number of live identities and freezes all of them when any one is flagged, forcing the operator to absorb the loss. An attacker must therefore acquire and risk a fresh sponsor account per batch, multiplying overhead by the batch size.
